Visit note | 2025-12-21 04:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Rahim Bepari, 38, male. Mr. Bepari attends for review and describes experiencing a persistent fear of dying despite having received normal heart test results. Visit note | 2025-12-23 03:00 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Hasan Kabir, 22, male. Mr. Kabir comes in for a review regarding his ear symptoms, explaining that his ear feels blocked and his hearing is muffled since he caught a cold. He states that the issue began after a cold during a trip to Khilgaon. He works as a police constable, which often exposes him to outdoor dust and fluctuating weather, and lives in a bustling area of the city. He has no known chronic comorbidities such as diabetes or hypertension. He denies any severe dizziness, facial weakness, or spontaneous bleeding from the canal, though he does report mild throbbing discomfort when pressing on the tragus. On clinical examination, his vital signs are notable for a temperature 101.2°F, alongside BP 116/75 mmHg, pulse 106 bpm, and weight 85 kg. Examination of the affected ear reveals an erythematous, bulging tympanic membrane with reduced mobility on pneumatic otoscopy, while the contralateral ear appears normal. The nasal mucosa is congested with mild post-nasal drip. Assessment: Acute otitis media. Plan: a prescription was issued for targeted management. He was strongly advised to keep the ear dry at all times, avoid inserting cotton buds or any foreign objects into the canal, and complete the full course of therapy. Follow-up is scheduled in 1 week to reassess membrane healing and hearing acuity.
